title: Hummingbird Feeder Surge and Refill Forecast
dataSources: Bird acoustic detections (`birdnet:detection`), wildlife-camera visits (`wildlifecam:visit`), nest-box state (`nestbox:event`), frog-call activity (`frogcall:detection`), and pollinator counts (`pollinator:count`).
app: Wildlife telemetry from BirdNET, trail and feeder cameras, nest-box sensors, frog-call detectors, and pollinator counters streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted imports.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=birdnet:detection species="hummingbird"
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as visits by feeder _time
| eventstats avg(visits) as avg_visits by feeder
| eval refill_risk=if(visits>avg_visits*1.5,"high","normal")
description: Flags days when hummingbird visits surge above each feeder's norm, suggesting nectar will run out sooner.
value: Visit spikes are fun to watch but easy to under-serve, so this helps turn activity into a practical refill plan.
implementation: Track hummingbird detections or feeder-visit counts with a feeder identifier and compare them against rolling averages.
visualization: Timeline of daily hummingbird visits with refill-risk state.
grandmaExplanation: It ranks when hummingbird traffic is so high that the feeder may need topping up sooner than usual.
